report.question: Do released artifacts, error messages, stack traces and logs disclose the owner's username, home path, machine name, private repository names or internal hostnames?
report.answer: YES for three of the five identity classes, and the two mechanisms need DIFFERENT fixes. (1) The BUILT bundle discloses only the USERNAME, and the two-profile differential proves every one of those 22 hits is HARDCODED (byte-identical archive across profiles) - author field, LICENSE holder, and 19 schema $id URIs on the owner-derived domain prekzursil.dev. (2) The RUNTIME surface is where the HOME PATH leaks, invisibly to any static scan: 5 of 21 error-message cases and 4 of 9 identity-token-free cases printed C:\Users\Prekzursil\..., and an unhandled exception prints a full traceback naming the absolute install path three times while exiting with a bare 1. (3) The log redactor strips credentials but has no identity rule, so a logged path ships verbatim. (4) MACHINE NAME was not emitted on any measured surface. (5) PRIVATE REPO NAMES and INTERNAL HOSTNAMES appear only in the release/ staging workspace (74 identity occurrences, 127.0.0.1:8089, localhost:4000), which the current payload projection does NOT ship. || RUN-2 + CROSS-VENDOR REVIEW: an independent openai/Codex refuter re-derived the measurement from the raw bundle and agreed on every headline number. Two changes were accepted: D1 rises to P1 because _emit at cli.py:391 sits OUTSIDE main()'s try/except, so an ordinary user pointing --json at a directory gets a raw traceback disclosing the absolute install path - no code injection needed; and `rg` without --hidden undercounts the username members as 21 because it skips .claude-plugin. One refuter claim was refuted in turn: `ast-integrate` (27 members) is NOT a private repository name - no such repo exists, and 0 of 16 private and 0 of 57 public repo names appear in the shipped bundle.
